title: Nvidia's unifying theory: full-stack accelerated computing, AI factories, Groq and open horizontals
summary: Post-GTC 2026 interview with Ben Thompson. Huang explains why Nvidia is an accelerated computing company, not a chip or GPU company. He covers building vertically then opening horizontally, the Groq deal, CPUs for agents, and why he opposes doomerism and bundling the AI stack.

principles.text: Start from what you need to become, not what you are not; hard problems need full-stack solutions.
principles.quote: my mind doesn’t start with, “What I’m not”, it starts with, “What do we need to be?”.

principles.text: Accelerate the application, not the chip. Nvidia is an accelerated computing company, not a GPU company.
principles.quote: We’re not obsessed about where computing is done, we just want to accelerate the application. Remember, Nvidia is an accelerated computing company, not a GPU company.

principles.text: A company moves fast when the CEO supplies a unifying theory and builds an organism that delivers it.
principles.quote: The reason why Nvidia can move so fast is because we always have a unifying theory for the company, and that’s my job

principles.text: Build vertically, integrate and optimize, then open it horizontally so others can use any piece.
principles.quote: We create a thing vertically and then we open it horizontally and so everybody could use whatever piece they would like.

principles.text: Great products come from feeling the pain point yourself and knowing where the market will go.
principles.quote: I think most great products are kind of because you see a pain point and you feel the pain point and you know that that’s where the market’s going to go.

principles.text: Teams that don't talk over-design their parts; working as one team pushes the limits.
principles.quote: When you have a lot of people who don’t talk to each other, integrate systems, you have to, by definition, over-design your part of it.
